ben-scott-mount-pleasant-1905-08-19.A1:
IS KILLED BY DEPUTIES
Negro Resisted Officers at Mt. Pleasant and Received Fatal Wounds.
Mount Pleasant, Tex., Aug. 22.—A negro, known as Ben Scott, died in the county jail Sunday night from a bullet wound he received in a pitched battle with Constable Meek and Deputy Hanes at his home eight miles north of town the night before.

The officers went to arrest him on a charge of assault to murder, committed on his wife, and when they reached his house he was not at home, but arrived while the officers were there. As soon as he saw them he ran into the house, got his pistol and came to the door and opened fire. A regular battle followed in which the negro emptied his pistol, and the officers fired a number of shots each. After the negro was wounded and his pistol empty, he ran to another house near by and endeavored to secure a winchester, but failing to do so he surrendered and was brought to town and lodged in jail. Before he died it was ascertained that he had gone by another name, probably John Johnson or Sam Brown, and it is believed that he was wanted in Louisiana for the murder of a white man. Several old bullet wounds were found on his body after death. It is stated that he had lived in this county for two years, but had never been to town, and in that way had avoided the officers.

He was about 5 feet, 10 inches in height, weighed about 185 pounds, and was almost black. He had an old bullet wound in the forehead, one on the right forearm and one on the right side. A negro woman who was living with him stated that his right name is Sam Brown and that he was wanted near Shreveport for the killing of a white man.

comfort-comfort-1905-08-21.A1:
NEGROES FROM COMORFT REACH SAN ANTONIO
Mitchell Garcia, one of the negroes who came to San Antonio yesterday as a result of the excitement at Comfort over an alleged insult by a negro dishwasher at the Good Times Inn to the daughter of a German citizen in the vicinity, called at the Ligut office thi, morning and gave his side of the story. Besides Garcia, there were in the party who took French leave of Comfort, his wife; Ernest Center, the cook; Claiborne Stovall, a waiter; Mrs. H. Plummer and daughter Elsie; and Oscar Bates, the negro who is alleged to have given the insult.

Garcia, who represented the party this morning, said:

"We left Comfort because we were not satisfied with the protection offered to us. A lot of men got together and looked ugly at us and we felt that things didn't look right. We think they took snap judgment over Bates, as we didn't think he meant to be disrespectful to the young lady. When we left Comfort, that cleaned the town of colored people. It is not a very healthy locality for the darky to try to live in.

"Bates, why they didn't give him no time to think. The first thing we knew was when they demanded that he come out and give himself up. Instead of doing this he took to his heels and ran down the railroad track. Bates himself says that he ran so fast that he didn't know whether he 'was running or a-flying.'"

"We are in good old San Antonio now, and we are going to stay here in the future. No more Comfort for us. Why do you know that in some of the towns way north of here there are signs nailed up at the depot platforms reading 'Nigger don't let the sun go down on you here?' There were two shots fired at Oscar Bates as he was making a hot-foot down the track."
comfort-comfort-1905-08-21.A2:
NEGRO ESCAPED.
Eight Germans Intended to Lynch Dishwasher, but He Got Away.

San Antonio, Aug. 22.—At Comfort eight enraged German citizens, armed with guns, visited the Good Times inn, demanded and secured a negro dishwasher employed there. They took him to the woods, where he escaped in some manner unknown. Several reports of firearms were heard from the direction of the woods. The cause of the attempt to lynch him is said to have been an insult to a daughter of a German citizen in the vicinity of the inn.

The incident freig!tened all negroes from Comfort and the inn was left without help. Guests to the number of fifty or sixty considered it a great lark to help with the preparation of the Sunday dinner. Manager Stanley of the inn has secured all the help he requires from this city, however, and the inconvenience to guests was temporary and was enjoyed.

phelp-bunyan-tuscaloosa-1905-08-19.A1:
LYNCHING IS FEARED
ARMED POSSEK IN PURSUIT OF BLACK BRUTE.
Phelp Bunyan Attempted to Assault Young Woman Near Tuscaloosa and Authorities Anticipate Attempt at Mob Violence.
Tuscaloosa, Aug. 20.—(Speoial.)—News has been received here that Miss Annie Barger, a young woman living some twenty miles north of this city, was boldly assaulted yesterday by a burly young negro some 18 years old, by the name of Phelp Bunyan, almost in speaking distance of her home where her aged parents live.

Miss Barger had gone to the spring after water when Bunyan made his appearance. He immediately seized her and was in the act of accomplishing his purpose when with all her strength she struggled with him, screaming as she did so.

He at last became frightened and made his escape through the heavy undergrowth. Armed men are in pursuit of the wretch and if caught he will doubtless be dealt with. It was reported that the negro was in Brookwood late yesterday and was thought to be coming towards Tuscaloosa. The Sheriff has been notified and begun a search.

A telephone message from Brookwood late last night stated that John Harmon, a young man of 30 years, was found on the road side at East Brookwood literally riddled with bullets. Near the place was found an empty shotgun, which was probably the means of his death. No satisfactory particulars have been received here but it is thought that he was shot by an assassin from the undergrowth and that the gun was left there simply as

ARMED POSSE AFTER
TUSCALOOSA NEGRO
BOLD ATTACK IS MADE ON MISS ANNIE BARGER AND NEGRO IS FRIGHTENED AWAY BY HER SCREAMS.
Tuscaloosa, August 20.—(Special.)—News has been received here that Miss Annie Barger, a young woman living some twenty miles north of this city, was boldly assaulted yesterday by a burly young negro some 18 years old by the name of Phelp Bunyon, almost in speaking distance of her home where her aged parents live. Miss Barger had gone to the spring after water when Bunyon made his appearance. He immediately seized her and was in the act of accomplishing his purpose when her screams frightened him and he made his escape through the heavy undergrowth.

Armed men are in pursuit and if caught he will doubtless be summarily dealt with. It was reported that the negro was in Brookwood late yesterday and was thought to be coming towards Tuscaloosa. The sheriff has joined in the search.
phelp-bunyan-tuscaloosa-1905-08-19.A3:
Negro Attacks White Girl.
Miss Barger, a young white girl, living about 20 miles from Tuscaloosa, Ala., was assaulted by Philip Binin, a young negro, last Sunday. Miss Barger was at the spring, where she had gone for water, only a short distance from the house, when Binin appeared. He seized his prey, when she, by all her strength and screems, frightened him, away.

Miss Barger's parents are quite aged, and before assistance could be rendered the negro made good his escape. It is thought that he is coming in the direction of Tuscaloosa, and the sheriff and his deputies are making search. If he is caught he will probably be severely dealt with.
phelp-bunyan-tuscaloosa-1905-08-19.A4:
Negro Assailant Arrested.
Tuscaloosa, August 24. — (Special.)— Phelp Binion, charged with attempting an assault on Mrs. Joseph Cunningham at her home last week, was arrested at Holt yesterday and brought to the city and placed in jail. Mrs Cunningham was engaged in washing when she was assaulted by Binion, a young negro who had been working around the place for some while. but her screams frightened him away. It was last week that the crime was committed and Binion left immediately for Brookwood and afterwards went to Holt, where he signed for work under an assumed name. He claims that he is not guilty of the charge.

william-curtis-saratoga-1905-08-13.A1:
STRIKES DOWN AGED PAIR
NEGRO KILLED IN CHASE.
New-York Rector and Wife Expected to Die from Injuries.
[BY TELEGRAPH TO THE TRIBUNE.]

Saratoga, N. Y., Aug. 13.—The Rev. and Mrs. Bernard Schulte, both over sixty-five years of age, of New-York City, were attacked at Mechanicsville last night and probably fatally injured by William Curtis, a negro, who was to-day shot and killed here while resisting arrest.

Mr. Schulte went to Mechanicsville recently to take charge of St. Luke's Episcopal Church during the absence of the rector, Dr. Oliver Shaw Nowell, who is now in Europe. Early last evening Curtis, whose home is in Saratoga, presented himself at the door of the rectory and asked for a drink of water. As Mr. Schulte was turning back to get the water the negro drew a piece of iron gas pipe from beneath his coat and felled the clergyman with a terrific blow on the head, following this up with blows until his victim lay unconscious and apparently dead.

Mrs. Schulte, who was upstairs, hurried down on hearing her husband fall, and was met in the hall by the negro, who struck her down before she could be beaten, and continued beating her with his heavy weapon until he had inflicted injuries from which she can hardly recover.

The clergyman and his wife were soon afterward discovered, lying unconscious and covered with blood, by neighbors, and a search was made for the negro, who had been as as he was leaving the house. Curtis robbed the rectory, and then, eluding his pursuers, walked twenty miles to this place, reaching town late late this forenoon and secreted himself in the Harris tenement house near West Congress-st. He was trailed by Detective James Sullivan and other officers. When found, he shot at Sullivan, and turned to run, when Sullivan fired, shooting him through the head. Curtis died in an ambulance on the way to the Saratoga Hospital.

Curtis was born in New-York thirty-two years ago, and for the last three or four years had been employed as a coal and lumber yard laborer here, also at Mechanicsville and Ballston Spa.

Albany, Aug. 13.—It is reported here that a motive of the attack upon Dr. and Mrs. Shulte, at Mechanicsville, may be found in the fact that Curtis's wife had been employed in the family of Dr. Newell, but was not engaged by the Schultes.

The Rev. Dr. William Everett Johnson, rector of the Church of the Redeemer, at No. 142 West 137th st., said last night that Dr. Schulte had been curate of the Church of the Redeemer about a year, living at No. 294 Central Park West. Mrs. Schulte, Dr. Johnson said, was a daughter of Coadjutor Bishop Nelson of Albany.

Two months ago, Dr. Johnson said, Dr. Schulte and his wife went to Mechanicsville, where Dr. Schulte was to supply a parish. Dr. Schulte was expected to return to the city and resume his duties as curate of the Church of the Redeemer next month.
william-curtis-saratoga-1905-08-13.A2:
NEGRO BURGLAR SHOT DEAD.
Assaults the Rev. Dr. and Mrs. Schulte and Is Killed Resisting Arrest.
SARATOGA, N. Y., Aug. 13.—William Curtis, while attempting to escape arrest here to-day, was shot and killed by Detective James Sullivan. About 9:30 o'clock Curtis, armed with an iron pipe eighteen inches long, forced an entrance into the rectory of St. Luke's Episcopal Church at Mechanicsville and murderously assaulted the Rev. Dr. Schulte and his wife, both of whom are 64 years old. They are in a critical condition.

The negro, whose main object was robbery, escaped from the building and started to walk to Saratoga Springs, a distance of twenty miles. He arrived late this morning. Detectives found him secreted in a house. When the negro sought to escape and placed his hand on his hip pocket Detective Sullivan fired. Curtis dropped and died soon after.

The Rev. Dr. Schulte has during the summer supplied St. Luke's Episcopal Church in Mechanicsville, the rector, the Rev. Dr. Newell, being on a European trip. Mrs. Schulte is said to be a sister of the wife of Bishop Doane of the diocese of Albany.

Curtis was a native of New York and for the past two or three years had been employed in coal and lumber yards in Mechanicsville, Saratoga Springs and Ballston Spa, and was well known in this section.

Mr. Schulte came to Mechanicsville recently to take charge of the Episcopal church during the absence of the rector, Dr. Oliver Shaw Newell, who is now in Europe. Early in the evening William Curtis, a negro, whose home is in Saratoga, presented himself at the door of the rectory and asked for a drink of water. Mr. Schulte was in the act of turning back to get the water when the negro drew a piece of lead pipe from beneath his coat and felled the clergyman with a terrific blow on the head, following this up with a rain of blows until his victim lay unconscious and apparently dead. Mrs. Schulte, who was upstairs, hurried down on hearing her husband fall and was met in the hall by the negro, who instantly struck her down before she could utter an outcry, and continued beating her with his heavy weapon until he had inflicted injuries from which she can hardly recover.

The clergyman and his wife were soon afterward discovered, lying unconscious and covered with blood, by neighbors, and a search was made for the negro, who had been seen leaving the house.

Rev. Schulte and Mrs. Schulte Are Perhaps Fatally Injured By Lead Pipe in Hands of Negro Brute.
THE ASSAILANT IS SHOT
Balliston, N. Y., August 13.—The Rev. B. Schulte and his wife were attacked at Mechanicsville last night and probably fatally injured by a negro who was today shot and killed in Saratoga while resisting arrest.

Early last Friday evening William Curtis, a negro, whose home is in Saratoga, presented himself at the door of the rectory and asked for a drink of water. Mr. Schulte was in the act of turning back to get the water, when the negro drew a piece of lead pipe from beneath his coat and felled the old clergyman with a terrific blow on the head, following this up with a rain of blows until his victim lay unconscious and apparently dead. Mrs. Schulte, who was upstairs, hurried down on hearing her husband fall, and was met in the hall by the negro who struck her down, inflicting injuries from which she can hardly recover. The clergyman and his wife were discovered lying unconscious and covered with blood by neighbors and a search was made for the negro who had been seen leaving the house.
Policeman James Sullivan discovered Curtis today in a negro colony in Saratoga and arrested him. The negro broke away and ran and after firing one shot in the air to halt him, Sullivan fired again, shooting the negro through the head and killing him instantly.

The injuries of Mr. and Mrs. Schulte were said tonight to be very serious.

william-curtis-saratoga-1905-08-13.A24:
RECOVER FROM ASSAULT.
SARATOGA, Aug. 26.—The Rev. Dr. and Mrs. Barnard Schulte, who two weeks ago were murderously assaulted in the St. Luke's Church rectory, in Mechanicsville, have so far recovered as to be able to return to their New York house, 237 Central Park West. They were attacked by William Curtis, a New York colored man, who was fatally shot by a Saratoga detective while resisting arrest.
